title: The $8 Million Shark That Secretly Got Replaced
description: AI-narrated commentary: the true story of one of the most expensive (and controversial) artworks ever sold, and the detail most people never hear about. #arthistory #shorts

hook_candidates.text: In 1991, an artist paid six thousand pounds for a dead tiger shark — and made it the most expensive dead animal in art history.
Nearly a million animals have died to become someone's art collection.
Would you still call it art if it cost the lives of a million animals?
That shark in the tank isn't the original — most people have no idea it was secretly replaced.

beats.text: He sealed it in a tank of formaldehyde and called it art.

beats.text: A billionaire later paid eight million dollars for it.

beats.text: One problem: sharks don't preserve like taxidermy. Within years the skin wrinkled and the tank turned cloudy.
beats.broll_query: decaying preserved specimen cloudy glass tank close up

beats.text: So the studio quietly caught a second shark and swapped it in — same title, same price tag, different animal.

beats.text: That's just one piece. Across his career, this artist's work has used hundreds of thousands of animals.
